title: lock: stop fingerprint scans while the display is blanked

leads.summary: Screen removal also re-arms fingerprint scans, even if no lit or real display remains
leads.consequence: On a locked machine with a blanked panel that drops its connection (HPD loss, dock unplug), onScreensChanged clears displaysBlank and starts fingerprint PAM without checking hasRealScreen() or actual DPMS. A zero-output lock can therefore scan with nobody able to see the lock; on a fast-failing reader, unsuccessful attempts can retry at 250 ms until the newly armed 5 s timer fires. Repeated screen changes can repeatedly postpone the stop. This undermines the PR's thermal gate specifically on problematic monitor transitions; a screen removal is not a wake. Keep the stopped state for removals/no lit outputs, or gate on independently confirmed panel state.
leads.triage: corroborates Opus R1-F2 residual; confirmed via Opus followup-1 Q1

leads.summary: Clean merge with #10130 leaves the fingerprint gate closed after an activity-only DPMS wake
leads.consequence: #10130 adds an IdleMonitor for an input that wakes Hyprland DPMS but never reaches LockView. On its first such event after blanking, #10130 restarts the blank timer without calling runWake or clearing displaysBlank; this PR has already stopped fingerprintRetryTimer and startFingerprint still rejects scans. The lock screen can now be visible for up to five seconds with the fingerprint reader idle, then reblank. The other PR is GitHub MERGEABLE on quattro; a git merge-file using this PR's base produces no markers, keeps both sides, and both static tests pass. Integrate that new wake route with the gate when either PR merges.
leads.triage: confirmed: coordinator read #10130 diff (handleActivityResumed only arms timer); Opus followup-1 Q2 traced combined behaviour

leads.summary: Screen-change rearm bypasses pending fingerprint backoff from #11918
leads.consequence: If open PR #11918 merges, a failed PAM run schedules a delayed exponential retry (Quickshell emits both error and completed(Error), so #11918 increments twice). A screen-change event after the error, before that timer fires, calls startFingerprint directly; with PAM no longer active it starts immediately, leaving the delayed timer pending and defeating the cooling interval. This is most relevant to a blanking HDMI panel repeatedly disappearing/reappearing, the exact class of monitor events the new handler watches. Put the screen handler through the same retry policy, or cancel the pending timer only for a confirmed user wake. #12544's different backoff is itself overwritten by its completed(Error) handler, so is not relied upon here.
leads.triage: conditional on #11918 merging; not verified behaviourally

leads.summary: #11273 implements the same blank-time fingerprint policy with incompatible abort semantics
leads.consequence: #11273 suspends on blank by aborting the current PAM conversation and using fingerprintSuspended, whereas this PR explicitly preserves in-flight scans and guards displaysBlank. Their separate heads both merge against quattro but are not stacked; merging them against the common base produces three Service.qml conflicts (runWake/runBlank, startFingerprint, screensChanged). Resolving by keeping either side alone discards the other's explicit abort/no-abort trade-off and gate, so the maintainers must pick a policy and reconcile both sets of checks before both can land.
leads.triage: already in Opus final (#11273 conflict); conflict regions corrected by self-check

leads.summary: #8581's screen-change blank backoff conflicts with this PR's two wake/blank hunks
leads.consequence: #8581 adds a 5/15/30 s screen-change reblank backoff for HPD-flapping monitors, resetting its counter on runWake and logging runBlank. It is already marked CONFLICTING against current quattro. Merge-file against that PR's own merge-base blob yields conflicts in runWake and runBlank. Accepting only #8581's runWake side while retaining this PR's later wasBlank use leaves wasBlank undefined; accepting only #8581's runBlank side drops the new fingerprintRetryTimer.stop() and the blank gate's state write. A conflict resolution must retain both policies or choose one deliberately.
leads.triage: verified #8581 exists (CONFLICTING vs quattro, blank backoff); distinct from #8531 in Opus list; low value

leads.summary: Hardware-authentication instructions omit the new wake-before-fingerprint limitation
leads.consequence: The manual tells enrolled users they can unlock with a fingerprint and that locking blanks the display, without warning that once the current PAM attempt finishes after blank, a finger on a dark display no longer starts a scan. The description documents this trade-off, but the published user instructions do not. Add a sentence to hardware authentication or the lock-screen manual to wake the panel before touching the reader once it is blank; do not imply all fingerprint hardware loses immediately while an in-flight verification still runs.
leads.triage: factual text verified (manual lines exist, generic); low value

## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

Follow-up on head `d54116f9`, reassessing the [previous review](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12420#issuecomment-5831010621) of `939ab0b6`.

**Verified:** the new commit fixes the per-event re-arm, re-arms the reader and the blank timer on screen changes, and the description now documents the healthy-reader trade-off. It also breaks an existing repository test (new finding below). The wake route through locked key binds is still open.

| Previous finding | Status at `d54116f9` |
|---|---|
| Wakes that bypass `runWake()` leave the reader off | Screen-change route resolved (`onScreensChanged` now calls `startFingerprint()`). Locked-key route still present, see below |
| Screen change while blanked restarts scanning with panels off | Resolved: `armBlankTimer()` re-blanks about 5 s after a screen change. Scanning resumes until that re-blank, and screen-change signals repeating faster than every 5 s keep postponing it, so it ends about 5 s after the last one. For scanning this is no worse than the base, which scans throughout |
| Touch-to-unlock from a blanked lock changes for every reader | Resolved as suggested: stated in the new "Trade-off on healthy readers" section |
| `runWake()` re-arms on every pointer and key event | Resolved: the `wasBlank` gate re-arms only on a blank-to-awake transition |
| Stale comment at `Service.qml:496-498` | Resolved: rewritten. Nit: the new text says the reader is "paused" while blanked, but a session already in flight keeps running |

**Verified:** the opening points of the previous review still hold at this head: `fingerprintPam.start()` has one call site, every trigger (now including `onScreensChanged`) goes through `startFingerprint()`, an in-flight session continues after blank, and unlock paths clear `lockRequested` before waking. The PR merges cleanly onto current `quattro` (`c231097d`), and the `quattro` commits since the merge-base do not touch the fingerprint, blank or wake code.

### New: `test/shell.d/video-background-test.sh` fails at this head

The assertion "the lock screen stops playback once displays go dark or power-saver is active" (lines 165-173) matches `root.displaysBlank = false` as the first statement of `runWake()`:

```js
/function runWake\(\) \{\s*\n\s*root\.displaysBlank = false/.test(lockService)
```

The new first line `var wasBlank = root.displaysBlank` (`Service.qml:178`) breaks that match.

```text
revision                          video-background-test.sh
merge-base d174d4aa               ok
previous head 939ab0b6            runWake first-line check passes
head d54116f9                     not ok
head merged into quattro          not ok
```

In a full `test/shell` run (244 files), the base and the head fail the same 7 unrelated files. The head fails only this one in addition.

**Impact:** `./test/shell` reports a new failure. The check is a text pattern: `runWake()` still clears `displaysBlank` (`Service.qml:179`), so the playback behaviour it guards is unchanged.

**Suggested change:** update the test's `runWake` pattern to allow the `wasBlank` line. Alternatively, keep `root.displaysBlank = false` as the first statement and move the re-arm into an `onDisplaysBlankChanged` handler for the true-to-false transition, which also covers the `onScreensChanged` route in one place. A copy of the head with that handler passes this test and the other lock-source text tests that ran in the sandbox (compositor-dependent tests skipped). Its QML behaviour was not run.

### Still present: panels lit by locked key binds leave the reader off

Keys bound with `{ locked = true }` (volume, brightness and media keys in `default/hypr/bindings/media.lua`, the power key in `utilities.lua:9`) light the panels through `key_press_enables_dpms = true` (`default/hypr/input.lua:72`). Hyprland claims a bound key, so it never reaches the lock surface:

```text
locked-bind key on a blanked lock, after the session in flight at blank has ended
  Hyprland: DPMS on, key consumed by the bind
  LockView: no key event -> no wakeRequested -> runWake() not called
  displaysBlank stays true -> startFingerprint() returns early
  result: lit lock showing the fingerprint icon, touch ignored
          until pointer motion or an unbound key
```

The session in flight at blank is not aborted and can run up to 30 s (pam_fprintd's default timeout), so this applies once it has ended.

Omarchy's own notes (commit `41b6cc69` and the comment at `Service.qml:35-38`) say a resume that keeps the same outputs also lights panels without `runWake()`. The same state would follow after resuming from a lock that had already blanked. If the outputs are re-created instead, `onScreensChanged` re-arms the reader. This resume route follows from source and was not observed on hardware.

**Impact:** once the in-flight session has ended, "press power, touch" on laptops with a sensor in the power button stops working until other input. "Open lid, touch" after a blanked lock would likely behave the same when the resume keeps the same outputs (not observed). No lockout or security impact. The trade-off section describes a "fully dark lock screen", and the note "no behavior change while the display is awake" does not hold for these routes.

**Suggested change:** mention the lit-lock case in the trade-off section, or gate on actual DPMS state as already listed for follow-up. Open PR #10130 adds an `IdleMonitor` whose `handleActivityResumed()` also sees this input but only calls `armBlankTimer()`. Combined with this PR, the lock would light for about 5 s with the reader off, then blank again. Routing that handler through `runWake()` while `displaysBlank` is set would re-arm the reader for locked-bind keys (not for resume), at the cost of running `omarchy-system-wake` on that input too.

**Related open PRs:** #11273 ("keep fingerprint idle while the display is blanked") targets the same behaviour with abort-on-blank semantics and conflicts textually with this PR in `runWake`, the `startFingerprint` guard and the blank-timer comment. The description's "libfprint#7179" refers to Omarchy PR #7179.
